dataset_metadata.title: Comprehensive Mine Planning and Scheduling Knowledge Base
dataset_metadata.description: Production-grade mine planning dataset covering open pit and underground methods, financial modeling, scheduling optimization, and East African case studies
dataset_metadata.author: Mining AI Knowledge Engine

cut_off_grade.definition: The minimum grade of mineralisation required for ore to be processed at a profit, covering all direct mining costs, processing costs, general and administrative (G&A) costs, and sustaining capital expenditure
cut_off_grade.economic_basis: Cut-off grade is the break-even point where revenue from recovered metal exactly equals total costs of extracting and processing the material

formula.general_expression: COG = (C_mining + C_processing + C_GA + C_sustaining_capex) / (R × P_metal × CF)

variables.C_mining: Total mining cost per tonne of ore mined (includes drilling, blasting, loading, hauling, grade control)
variables.C_processing: Total processing cost per tonne of ore treated (includes comminution, concentration, leaching, CIL, gravity, flotation)
variables.C_GA: General and administrative cost per tonne of ore (includes camp, labour, management, office, regulatory compliance)
variables.C_sustaining_capex: Sustaining capital expenditure per tonne (includes equipment replacement, tailings dam raises, infrastructure maintenance)
variables.R: Metallurgical recovery rate (fraction, e.g., 0.95 for 95% recovery)
variables.P_metal: Commodity spot or long-term forecast price per unit
variables.CF: Conversion factor to convert grade to the same units as price

derived_formulas.whittle_cog: COG_w = COG_be + profit_margin_factor × (Revenue_per_tonne - COG_be × R × P × CF)

open_pit.notes: Costs increase exponentially with strip ratio; truck and shovel vs. dragline significantly affects cost

underground.notes: Underground costs vary by method, depth, ground conditions, and production rate

pressure_oxidation.notes: Required for refractory ores; significantly higher CAPEX and OPEX

conversion_factor_oz_per_tonne.notes: 1 gram = 0.0321507 troy ounces; 1 troy ounce = 31.1035 grams

maximize_NPV.method: Set COG equal to marginal cost (processing + G&A + sustaining capex only)
maximize_NPV.description: Mining costs are sunk once material is blasted; only incremental costs matter for NPV maximization
maximize_NPV.when_to_use: When objective is to maximize present value of all cash flows
advantages: Accounts for time value of money

maximize_tonnage.method: Set COG equal to total average cost (all costs included)
maximize_tonnage.description: Ensures every tonne of ore processed covers its full share of all mine costs
maximize_tonnage.formula: COG_tonnes = (C_mining + C_processing + C_GA + C_sustaining_capex) / (R × P × CF)
maximize_tonnage.when_to_use: When mine is throughput-constrained and revenue per tonne is marginal

hybrid.method: Ramp COG upward as metal price increases; lower when price decreases
hybrid.description: Dynamic cut-off grade that responds to market conditions to balance NPV and risk
hybrid.when_to_use: Most common in practice; balances risk and value
disadvantages: May leave ore in marginal zones
Complex to implement in scheduling software

phased_approach.method: Different COG for different phases of the mine life
phased_approach.description: Uses higher COG in early years when debt servicing is critical, lower in later years

phases.early_life: High COG to maximize early cash flow for debt repayment
phases.mid_life: Moderate COG for steady production and shareholder returns
phases.late_life: Lower COG to extend mine life and maximize total recovery

geological_domain_based.method: Apply different COGs to different geological domains based on metallurgical response
geological_domain_based.description: Accounts for variability in mineralogy, hardness, and recovery across the deposit

domains.oxide_zone: Lower COG due to higher recovery and lower processing cost
domains.sulphide_zone: Higher COG due to refractory nature and lower recovery

gold_CIL_example.description: Typical gold deposit processed via CIL circuit
gold_CIL_example.interpretation: Ore above 0.57 g/t Au is profitable to process under these conditions

gold_heap_leach_example.description: Gold deposit processed via heap leach in arid environment
gold_heap_leach_example.interpretation: Lower processing cost but lower recovery results in different cut-off grade profile

copper_flotation_example.description: Porphyry copper deposit processed via flotation
copper_flotation_example.interpretation: Ore above 0.36% Cu is profitable to process

long_term_planning.definition: Strategic mine plan covering the full life of mine from exploration through closure, defining production targets, capital requirements, and economic returns

objectives: Obtain mining permits and environmental approvals
activities: Feasibility study completion and board approval
Water use permits and extraction licences
Land acquisition and resettlement action plans
Processing plant mechanical and electrical installation
Leach circuit or flotation circuit installation
CIL circuit or SX/EW plant construction
Quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) program
Processing plant operation at design capacity

pushback_scheduling.description: Sequencing extraction of nested pit shells to define phases of open pit mining
process: Run Lerchs-Grossmann or Pseudoflow optimization at multiple revenue factors
Generate nested pit shells (5-20 shells)
Define pushbacks as groups of nested shells
Schedule pushbacks in sequence based on NPV contribution
Apply mining rate and processing constraints
Optimize within pushbacks for grade blending

nested_pit_scheduling.description: Detailed scheduling within individual pit shells
process: Define mining blocks within each pit shell
Apply pushover constraints and slope angles
Schedule blocks to meet production targets
Account for mining equipment accessibility
Apply blending and stockpile rules
Define stope geometry based on geotechnical conditions
Optimize stope dimensions for maximum extraction
Schedule stopes based on grade, accessibility, and stress conditions
Plan development access for each stope
Sequence stoping to manage ground stress
Plan backfill operations

level_by_level.description: Underground mining sequence progressing from upper to lower levels
process: Develop top level first for early access
Complete stoping on upper level before proceeding down
Maintain vertical development advance ahead of stoping
Plan level development access and ventilation
Schedule level infrastructure installation
disadvantages: Later levels may have lower grades

bottom_up_sequencing.description: Starting mining from lower levels and progressing upward
bottom_up_sequencing.when_to_use: Deep deposits with high-grade ore at depth
advantages: Early access to high-grade deep ore
Lower initial mining costs if ore is deeper
Potential for sub-level caving from bottom

top_down_sequencing.description: Starting mining from surface and progressing to depth
top_down_sequencing.when_to_use: Most common approach for open pit and shallow underground

mine_life_optimization.methodology: Lane's algorithm for optimum cut-off grade scheduling
constraints: Market capacity (tonnes of product per annum)

pushback_principles.definition: A pushback is a phase of open pit mining that extracts a portion of the orebody in sequence, designed to maximize NPV while maintaining operational practicality

principles: Each pushback must be self-sustaining (revenue > cost)
Pushbacks should progress from highest to lowest NPV zones
Inner pushbacks typically have higher grades
Outer pushbacks may have lower grades and higher strip ratios
Pushback transitions must be smooth to avoid operational disruptions

bench_slope_angle.depends_on: Rock mass quality and blast damage

berm_width.notes: Required for safety and access; width depends on bench height and slope angle

algorithm.name: Lerchs-Grossmann
algorithm.type: Graph theory based maximum closure algorithm
algorithm.description: Finds the pit that maximizes total profit by identifying the set of blocks whose total revenue minus total cost is maximum, subject to slope constraints
algorithm.performance: Pseudoflow is generally faster for large block models; both produce identical results for standard problems

parameters.name: block_model
parameters.description: 3D block model with grade, rock type, density, and economic value attributes

parameters.name: revenue_blocks
parameters.description: Block values calculated from grade × recovery × price - selling costs
parameters.formula: V_block = Tonnage × Grade × Recovery × Price × Payable% - C_processing - C_GA - C_selling

parameters.name: slope_constraints
parameters.description: Maximum allowable slope angles in all directions
parameters.input_format: User-defined angles for each direction (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW) or single overall angle

parameters.name: mining_cost
parameters.description: Cost to mine each block (may vary by rock type, depth, or zone)

parameters.name: processing_cost
parameters.description: Cost to process each block (may vary by mineralogy)

parameters.name: discount_rate
parameters.description: Used for NPV optimization in dynamic scheduling

parameters.name: metal_price
parameters.description: Revenue per unit of metal produced
parameters.assumptions: May use spot price, long-term forecast, or price deck

outputs: Nested pit shells at various revenue factors
validation: Verify total ore tonnes match resource estimate
Ensure processing plant is fully utilized

gradient.typical_design: 10% sustained with 12% maximum over short distances
gradient.empty_trucks: Can handle steeper gradients on return haul
gradient.notes: Gradient is the primary constraint on truck productivity and fuel consumption

turning_radius.design_criterion: Minimum 3x truck length for safe turning

super_elevation.formula: e = v² / (g × R) where v = speed, g = gravity, R = curve radius

safety_features: Rolling barriers or concrete barriers on high-walls
Catch berms 60% of truck tire height minimum

rules_of_thumb: Minimum 2× blast hole diameter for proper breakage

bench_width_determination.combination_berms: Can combine operational and safety functions

bench_configuration.single_bench: One bench at a time, most common
bench_configuration.double_bench: Two benches combined for larger catch berm
bench_configuration.multi_bench: Multiple benches combined for final walls

surface_preparation.seal: Bitumen or polymer seal for dust control

design_traffic.traffic_volume: Based on fleet size and cycle time

applicable_conditions: Moderate to poor rock mass quality
Good to moderate rock mass quality
Good to excellent rock mass quality
Poor to moderate rock mass quality

factors: Wider stopes possible with cemented fill
Reduced number of levels lowers cost

sublevel_spacing.notes: Sublevels are intermediate levels used for drilling and access in sublevel stoping

principles: Extract high-grade stopes first for early cash flow
Maintain stress shadow to protect adjacent stopes
Ensure development access ahead of stoping
Allow time for backfill curing before adjacent stoping

primary_secondary.description: Alternate primary and secondary stopes; primary stopes backfilled before secondary extraction
primary_secondary.backfill: Cemented paste or rock fill for primary; uncemented for secondary

retreating.description: Mining progresses from one end of the orebody to the other
disadvantages: Later stopes may have lower grades

advancing.description: Mining progresses from multiple points toward a central area

staggered.description: Stopes are extracted in a staggered pattern to manage stress

decline.purpose: Primary access for equipment and personnel

decline_to_ore.purpose: Direct access from decline to ore zone

level_development.crosscut: Horizontal development from decline to orebody
level_development.drift: Development along the orebody on each level

stope_access.drawpoints: Extraction points at base of stope

infrastructure.loading_bays: Where ore is loaded for haulage

objectives: Provide fresh air to all working areas

exhaust.description: Main fan at surface exhausts air from mine

supply.description: Main fan at surface forces air into mine

auxiliary.description: Secondary fans to ventilate dead-end headings

fan_specification.control: Variable speed drive for energy optimization

cooling_requirements.cooling_capacity: 500-5000 kW depending on mine depth and size

monthly_target_formulation.objective: Define monthly ore tonnage, waste tonnage, grade, and metal production targets that achieve the annual plan while smoothing operations
constraints: Geological variability and grade control accuracy

decision_variables: Tonnes of ore from each block/zone per period
Tonnes of waste from each block/zone per period
linear_programming.constraints_matrix: A × x ≤ b, where A is constraint matrix, x is decision vector, b is RHS

heuristic_methods.description: Greedy algorithms, genetic algorithms, simulated annealing
heuristic_methods.application: Large-scale problems where exact methods are too slow

target_smoothing.method: Apply rolling average or moving window to monthly targets
target_smoothing.purpose: Reduce variability in operations and financial planning

decline.method: Progressive reduction in throughput or grade as reserves deplete

tonnage_grade_reconciliation.definition: Comparison between planned (modelled) and actual (mined) tonnage and grade to validate the resource model and mine plan

reconciliation_hierarchy.model_to_mill: Geological model vs. actual head grade to plant
reconciliation_hierarchy.model_to_mined: Geological model vs. blast hole grade control

reconciliation_methods.tagging_system: Unique IDs for each blast hole, truck load, and plant feed
reconciliation_methods.geostatistical_reconciliation: Compare kriged estimates with production data
reconciliation_methods.cumulative_reconciliation: Running total to identify systematic biases

common_issues.positive_reconciliation: Actual > Planned; may indicate model underestimation or selective mining
common_issues.negative_reconciliation: Actual < Planned; may indicate model overestimation, dilution, or ore loss
common_issues.grade_variability: Natural geological variation not captured in model
common_issues.dilution: Unplanned waste mixing with ore during mining

reporting.investor_reporting: Key metric for mining company disclosure

rom_stockpile.management: Maintain consistent grade blend to plant

low_grade_stockpile.purpose: Store material below current cut-off grade for future processing
low_grade_stockpile.typical_size: Months to years of future feed
low_grade_stockpile.management: Reassess periodically as cut-off grade changes

marginal_stockpile.purpose: Store material near cut-off grade for blending
marginal_stockpile.management: Blend with higher grade ore to maintain target grade

high_grade_stockpile.purpose: Store high-grade ore for strategic blending or when plant capacity is limited
high_grade_stockpile.management: Priority feed to plant during grade control

waste_stockpile.purpose: Store waste material for future reprocessing or backfill

stockpile_economics.opportunity_cost: Value of metal locked in stockpile at discount rate

optimization.method: Determine optimal stockpile size to maximize NPV while maintaining mill feed continuity

blending_strategies.objective: Achieve target head grade and mineralogy at the processing plant by blending ore from different sources

grade_blending.description: Combine high and low grade ore to achieve target head grade
grade_blending.formula: Grade_target = (T₁ × G₁ + T₂ × G₂ + ... + Tₙ × Gₙ) / (T₁ + T₂ + ... + Tₙ)

mineralogy_blending.description: Blend ores with different mineralogy to optimize metallurgical response

contaminant_blending.limits: Set by smelter or environmental regulations

temporal_blending.description: Blend ore from different mining phases over time to smooth grade profile
temporal_blending.approach: Mine multiple pushbacks simultaneously with different grade profiles

spatial_blending.description: Blend ore from different parts of the deposit simultaneously
spatial_blending.approach: Load trucks from multiple faces and blend at ROM pad

blending_techniques.truck_blending: Load trucks from different faces and mix at ROM pad
blending_techniques.conveyor_blending: Use conveyor stacking and reclaiming for continuous blending
blending_techniques.inpit_blending: Blend ore from different benches during mining

where.CF_t: Net cash flow in year t

components.Re: Cost of equity (CAPM: Rf + β × (Rm - Rf))
components.Rd: Cost of debt (interest rate on borrowings)

incremental_NPV.description: NPV of each phase or pushback to determine optimal sequence
incremental_NPV.application: Compare pushback options, stope sequences, and expansion decisions

after_tax_NPV.formula: AT_NPV = Σ [(Revenue - Opex - Depreciation) × (1 - Tax_rate) + Depreciation - Capex - Working_capital_changes] / (1 + r)^t
after_tax_NPV.notes: Depreciation is added back as it is a non-cash expense

greenfield_gold.notes: Includes all capital and operating costs from scratch

brownfield_gold.notes: Leveraging existing infrastructure and processing facilities

greenfield_copper.notes: Large scale operations with significant capex

greenfield_coal.notes: Highly variable based on coal quality and market

lithium.notes: High demand driven by EV market

payback_period.target: 5 years or less for most projects
payback_period.formula: Payback = Year before recovery + (Unrecovered cost at start of year / Cash flow during year)
payback_period.notes: Undiscounted payback is most common; discounted payback should also be considered
payback_period.importance: Indicates how quickly initial capital is recovered; important for project financing

gold_price.impact: Directly affects revenue; most sensitive parameter

capital_expenditure.impact: Affects initial investment and ongoing sustaining costs

exchange_rate.impact: Affects cost base for non-USD operations

monte_carlo.description: Probabilistic analysis using random sampling of uncertain parameters
methodology: Define probability distributions for each uncertain variable

input_distributions.gold_price: Lognormal with mean = base case, σ = 15-25%
input_distributions.operating_cost: Normal with mean = base case, σ = 10-20%

scenario_analysis.description: Evaluate project under discrete scenarios representing different market or operational conditions

scenarios.optimistic: Best case: high price, high recovery, low cost
scenarios.pessimistic: Worst case: low price, low recovery, high cost
scenarios.stress_test: Extreme conditions to test project viability

decision_tree_analysis.description: Map sequential decisions and chance events
decision_tree_analysis.application: Evaluate exploration targets, expansion options, hedging strategies
decision_tree_analysis.method: Calculate expected value at each decision node

real_options_analysis.description: Value flexibility in mine plan (expand, contract, defer, abandon)
options: Option to defer (wait for higher prices)
real_options_analysis.method: Black-Scholes or binomial option pricing adapted for mining

revenue_calculation.formula: Revenue = Tonnage_milled × Grade × Recovery × Metal_price × Payable% - Treatment_charges - Refining_charges

C1_cash_cost.formula: C1 = (Mining_cost + Processing_cost + G&A + Transport + Royalties) / Ounces_produced

AISC.notes: All-in sustaining cost is the industry standard for comparing mining companies
